verdict: Avoid new printing & publishing exposure in Okhla; lend only to niche digital/packaging converters with clean receivables and input-price pass-through, and decline plain commercial offset printers.
title: Okhla printing & publishing: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
Okhla Phases I and II carry the bulk of the estate's printing presses alongside garments, packaging and machinery, while Phase III is corporate/IT space [1]. **A press buys paper and ink, runs it through offset or digital machines, and sells a job — the cash cycle is short but the asset is the machine.** Paper and ink are the key raw materials and operating profitability stays exposed to their prices [9]. So when a proposal lands, check the paper procurement contract and whether job contracts carry an escalation clause; if the customer cannot reprice on input moves, ask for the last two years' gross margin by job type.

## Where value and cash sit
**Value sits in the customer relationship and the machine, not in the building — Okhla rents run roughly ₹20–₹120 per sq ft per month depending on phase and building quality [1].** Working capital is the real risk: a rated peer carried NWC/OI of 41.1% in FY2025, improved from 43.3% in FY2024 [8]. So when a proposal lands, check debtor days against that 41.1% benchmark; if receivables stretch beyond it, ask for the aged debtor list and the top five buyers' payment history. Capex is continuous — publication businesses must keep upgrading infrastructure and technology [10] — so treat any request for fresh press capacity as a separate, fully appraised facility.

## What has changed now
**The local demand signal is weak: Delhi GST collections grew 2.7% Apr-to-date against India's 6.1%, and Delhi electricity demand grew 6.5% against India's 9.5% [D].** India-wide printing output (NIC 17) fell 0.1% YoY even as Apr-to-date output rose 8.6% [D]. The data-based call is AVOID at 37 [D]. Peer results are mixed and mostly outside Delhi: True Colors reported H1 FY27 revenue of ₹183.01 crore with 17.67% EBITDA margins [6], while Dachepalli's 13.9% net margin came in below its 14% guidance [7]. The OPPA training office in Okhla is dated October 2025 — over a year old [2][3]. Sources say little specific to Okhla printing volumes, so lean on first principles and these peers.

## Who to pursue, who to avoid
**Pursue digital-first converters and packaging-linked printers with contracted, repeat B2B buyers; avoid plain commercial offset job-shops bidding on price.** The education-linked segment shows stable demand and improving margins on better manufacturing efficiency and stable paper prices [8]. Repro's digital business grew about 16% YoY to roughly ₹394 crore in FY26 [5]. So when a proposal lands, check the share of revenue from contracted versus spot jobs; if spot jobs dominate, ask for the order book and decline if it is under one month.

## How to grow safely and what to watch
**Structure every line as a receivables-backed working capital facility with a monthly stock-and-debtor statement as a condition.** Take the paper purchase register and GST returns every month, and covenant that escalation clauses exist on all major contracts [9]. Watch for debtor days crossing the 41.1% NWC/OI benchmark [8], a fall in Delhi GST growth below the current 2.7% [D], and any press running below stated capacity.
watch: Debtor days above the 41.1% NWC/OI peer benchmark [8] -> freeze further drawing power and seek a receivables charge
Delhi GST growth slipping below 2.7% Apr-to-date [D] -> cut exposure limits on spot-job printers
Input cost rise with no escalation clause in customer contracts [9] -> reprice facility or demand margin support
Sharp fall in unit consumption versus stated capacity -> inspect plant and reassess
Printing peers reporting margin compression like the 13.9% vs 14% case [7] -> tighten new sanctions in that sub-segment
watch_note: Trigger levels are policy suggestions (analytical framing), not data.
news_why: Delhi GST and power demand both trail India; printing output down 0.1% YoY [D].
